title: Decontamination of Tooth Roots for Ancient DNA Extraction
author: Marcel Keller

steps.title: Clean hood and bench
steps.instruction: Wipe the drill hood and table bench surfaces with DNA Exitus, then rinse with water.

steps.title: Set up decontamination station
steps.instruction: Fill a 100 mL beaker with 1 × NaOCl (bleach, 6 % v/v), 1 × MilliQ water, and 1 × ethanol; keep the beaker on the bench.

steps.title: Place tools in bleach
steps.instruction: Put the toothbrush and tweezers into the bleach solution.

steps.title: Prepare labeled tubes
steps.instruction: For each sample, prepare two 50 mL tubes and label one “B” (bleach) and one “E” (ethanol) with the sample ID.

steps.title: Add bleach to B tubes
steps.instruction: Add approximately 5 mL of 6 % v/v NaOCl to each B tube, ensuring the sample will be fully submerged.

steps.title: Add ethanol to E tubes
steps.instruction: Add approximately 5 mL of 70 % ethanol to each E tube, ensuring the sample will be fully submerged.

steps.title: Arrange drying rack and UV
steps.instruction: Place paper towels on a drying rack (e.g., upside‑down multi‑rack lid), tape them in place, label with sample IDs, set the rack on a piece of aluminum foil inside the hood, and turn on the UV lamp.

steps.title: Bleach incubation (dirty samples)
steps.instruction: If the sample is visibly dirty, submerge it in its B tube for 5 minutes (00:05:00) while shaking intermittently.

steps.title: Dispose bleach and flush sink
steps.instruction: Pour excess NaOCl from the tubes down the sink with the faucet running to dilute the bleach, then keep the faucet running to flush any remaining bleach from the drain.

steps.title: Rinse with MilliQ water
steps.instruction: Rinse each sample three times with MilliQ water, shaking and discarding the wash each time.

steps.title: Ethanol incubation
steps.instruction: After the final water rinse, shake, discard excess water, then submerge the sample in its E tube for 2 minutes (00:02:00).

steps.title: Dispose ethanol and rinse sink
steps.instruction: Pour excess ethanol from the tubes into the sink, place the tubes back on the rack, and rinse the sink with faucet water when finished.

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: In the hood, place paper towels in front of the rack to catch ethanol; blot each tube to remove as much ethanol as possible before moving the sample onto the labeled square on the drying rack.

steps.title: UV‑dry samples
steps.instruction: Keep the UV lamp on while allowing the samples to dry for at least 2 hours (02:00:00) or overnight.

steps.title: Choose continuation or stop
steps.instruction: Either proceed immediately to the “ancient DNA extraction (chunk samples/high volume)” protocol, or stop here and prepare for later processing as described below.

steps.title: Prepare weighing boats and record weight
steps.instruction: For each sample, place a small weighing boat labeled with the sample ID, tare the balance with the boat, place the tooth or petrous core on it, record the weight, and transfer the sample to a 5 mL tube (suitable for ~250 mg).

steps.title: Set out medium weighing boats
steps.instruction: Put out one medium weighing boat for each sample and label it in the corner.

steps.title: Place sample in weighing boat
steps.instruction: Take the sample to be used for extraction and place it in the medium weighing boat labeled with its sample ID.

steps.title: Clean sample surface with bleach brush
steps.instruction: Gently remove surface dirt using the toothbrush soaked in NaOCl; avoid splashing bleach or dirt onto yourself or other samples.

steps.title: Change gloves as needed
steps.instruction: Replace gloves during the decontamination steps whenever they become dirty or wet.
